paper_metadata.title: A CMOS 10-Gb/s Power-Efficient 4-PAM Transmitter
paper_metadata.abstract: A novel power-efficient architecture for a multilevel pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) transmitter is proposed. A data-look-ahead technique is used to pre-switch the current sources so that drive current is reduced when transmitting small voltage levels. This technique also eliminates the need for a pre-driver block, which also saves transmitter power. Based on this architecture, a 4-PAM transmitter is designed in 0.18m standard digital CMOS technology. The transmitter achieves 3.5 GS/s (7 Gb/s) with a 1.7-V supply and 5 GS/s (10 Gb/s) with a 2-V supply and it occupies an area of 0.16 mm2. The output driver and the entire transmitter consume only 11.25 and 66 mW at 7 Gb/s (20 and 121 mW at 10 Gb/s), respectively, which are the lowest reported powers at this speed.
